-V/s- ACCUSED : 1. Mubarak  S/o. Nasir Ahamed,
 Aged 29 years, R/at. No.56,
 9th cross, Padarayanapura,
Jagajeevanram Nagar, Bengaluru.

2. Yogaraj  S/o. Gangaiah,
 Aged 34years, R/at. No.50,

 Magadi Road, Bengaluru.
 2 C.C.No.17865/2015  Date of Commission of 17.12.2013  offence  Date of report 20.12.2013  Date of arrest
On 30.11.2015, the accused No.1  and 2 appeared before the Court  and got enlarged themselves on  bail.

Opinion of the Judge

As per final orders Nagaraju V vs Mubharak on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144185975/
1  State Represented by Senior Asst.Public Prosecutor  Accused Represented by Sri.K.Elangovan -Advocate.
JUDGMENT [Delivered on 13.09.2024]
The PSI of Cubbon Park PS has filed charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable U/Sec.379, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 473 r/w 34 of IPC.

2. Brief facts of prosecution case is as follows:
The accused No.1 stolen Hero Honda Splendor motor cycle bearing No.KA.05.HK.8723 of CW.1 on 17.12.2013 in the afternoon, which was parked in the parking area of Cunningham cross road, Bengaluru and handed over the same to accused No.2.

In turn, the accused No.2 with an intention to cheat the general public changed its number as KA.06.ED.1436, created a RC book by tallying to its chassis and engine number, sold it to CW.8 for money, cheated him, used the forged RC book as a genuine document knowing fully well that, it is a forged document and changed the number plate of the vehicle with an intention to forge the document.

On the basis of written information given by CW.1, the Cubbon Park police have registered this case against the accused in Cr.No.270/2013.
3.
After the investigation, the IO filed charge sheet against the accused.

This Court has taken cognizance of the offences punishable U/Sec.379, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 473 r/w 34 of IPC.
4.
In response to the service of summons, on 30.11.2015, the accused No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court and got enlarged themselves on bail.
This Court complied with Sec.207 of Cr.P.C., and furnished charge sheet copies to the accused.
5. This Court heard both the parties.
As there were no grounds to discharge the accused, this Court framed charges for the offences punishable U/Sec.379, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 473 r/w 34 of IPC.
The accused did not plead guilty.
They claimed to be tried.
6. In order to prove its case, the prosecution got examined 6 witnesses as PW.1 to 6 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 9 documents.
After completion of prosecution side evidence, the statements of the accused were recorded U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C., wherein they denied the incriminating evidence led against them.
They did not choose to lead their defense evidence.
7. I have heard the arguments of Senior APP and Sri. K.E Advocate.

8. On the basis of allegations made against the accused, the following points arise for my consideration:
1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused No.1 in furtherance of common intention stolen Hero Honda Splendor motor cycle bearing Nagaraju V vs Mubharak on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144185975/
2 No.KA.05.HK.8723 of CW.1 on 17.12.2013 in the afternoon, which was parked in the parking area of Cunningham cross road, Bengaluru and handed over the same to accused No.2 and thereby they have committed the offence punishable U/Sec.379 R/w 34 of IPC?
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused in furtherance of common intention changed the number of the motor cycle as KA.06.ED.1436, cheated general public and thereby they have committed the offence punishable U/Sec.465 r/w 34 of IPC?
3.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused in furtherance of common intention created a RC book by tallying to the chassis and engine number of the motor cycle and thereby they have committed the offence punishable U/Sec.467 r/w 34 of IPC?

4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused in furtherance of common intention, created RC book for the purpose of cheating and thereby they have committed the offence punishable U/Sec.468 r/w 34 of IPC?

5. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused in furtherance of common intention dishonestly sold the stolen motor cycle to CW.8 for money and thereby they have committed the offence punishable U/Sec.420 r/w 34 of IPC?

6. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused in furtherance of common intention, used the forged RC book as a genuine document knowing fully well that, it is a forged document, handed over the same to CW.8 and thereby they have committed the offence punishable U/Sec.471 r/w 34 of IPC?
7.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused in furtherance of common intention, changed the number plate of the motor cycle with an intention to forge the document and thereby they have committed the offence punishable U/Sec.473 r/w 34 of IPC?
8. What order?

9. My answers to the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In Negative  Point No.2 : In Negative  Point No.3 : In Negative  Point No.4 : In Negative  Point No.5 : In Negative  Point No.6 : In Negative  Point No.7 : In Negative Nagaraju V vs Mubharak on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144185975/
3  Point No.8 : As per final orders for the following:
 REASONS Point No.1 to 7: As all these points are interrelated, I take all the seven points together for common discussion to avoid repetition.
10.

The burden is casted on the prosecution to prove that, the accused No.1 in furtherance of common intention stolen Hero Honda Splendor motor cycle bearing No.KA.05.HK.8723 of CW.1 on 17.12.2013 in the afternoon, which was parked in the parking area of Cunningham cross road, Bengaluru and handed over the same to accused No.2, they changed the number of the motor cycle as KA.06.ED.1436,
created a RC book by tallying to the chassis and engine number of the motor cycle for the purpose of cheating, dishonestly sold the stolen motor cycle to CW.8 for money,
used the forged RC book as a genuine document knowing fully well that, it is a forged document, handed over the same to CW.8 and changed the number plate of the motor cycle with an intention to forge the document.
11.

In order to prove its case, the prosecution got examined the complainant/CW.1 as PW.1, circumstantial witness/CW.2 as PW.2, mahazar witness /CW.3 as PW.3, CW.5 as PW.4, the officer, who registered the case CW.11 as PW.5 and investigation officer/CW.17 as PW.6 and got marked written information/complaint as Ex.P.1, spot mahazar as Ex.P.2, photographs as Ex.P.3 and 4, portion of the statement of PW.1 as Ex.P.5, report given by PW.5 as Ex.P.6, FIR as Ex.P.7, letter of PSI of Jagajeevanram Nagar police station as Ex.P.8 and fabricated RC as Ex.P.9.
12.
CW.1/PW.1 - Nagaraj in his evidence has stated that, he owned Hero Honda Splendor motor cycle.
He had given the same to his nephew/CW.2.
About 3 years ago, the CW.2 had parked his vehicle near Cubbon park and went for his work.
After completion of his work, when he returned to the spot, he did not find the bike.

Hence,
he along with CW.2 tried to search the same.
But they could not find it.
Hence, he gave Ex.P.1 complaint to the police.
Subsequently, the police visited the spot and drawn Ex.P.2 mahazar.
After a lapse of one year, the Cubbon park police called him to the station and showed his bike.
He noticed that the wheel and number plates of his bike are replaced.
The police did not show the offenders to him.
By executing an indemnity bond, he has taken the bike to his interim custody.
Ex . P.3
and 4 are the photographs of his motorcycle.

PW.2 - Sunil Kumar in his evidence has stated that, the CW.1 is his maternal uncle, who owned Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle bearing Nagaraju V vs Mubharak on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144185975/
4 No.KA.05.HK.8723.
The CW.1 had given the said motorcycle to him.
About 3 years ago on 17.12.2013, he had parked the said motorcycle at Cunningham cross road and been to his work.
When he returned to the spot, he could find the bike.
He searched for the bike and subsequently CW.1 gave a complaint to Cubbon Park police.
On 21.08.2021, Jagajeevanram Nagar police called him and CW.1 to their station and showed the bike.
At that time, they noticed the number plate of their bike is changed as KA.06.ED.1436.
The police neither showed that accused nor their photographs to them at the station.
They learnt that, the said motorcycle was sold to a person of Kunigal.
14. CW.3/PW.3 - Nandish in his evidence admits his signature found on Ex.P.2 mahazar.
The police have drawn Ex.P.2 mahazar at 2.30 p.m., to 3 p.m., at Cunningham cross road in connection with a theft of his friend's motorcycle.
At that time, he signed the said mahazar.

15. CW.5/PW.4 - Jagadish in his evidence has stated that, while he was working as constable at Cubbon park police station, a case was registered in their police station on 20.12.2013 regarding the theft of motorcycle.
The CW.17 took him to the spot along with CW.1, where he has drawn Ex.P.2 mahazar.
As per the dictation of CW.17, he has written the mahazer.

16. CW.11/PW.5 - Gajendra in his evidence has stated that, while he was working as Head constable at Jagajeevanram Nagar police station on 18.08.2014 the CW.16 deputed him and CW.12 to trace out the accused of Cr.No.122/2014 of their police station.

Accordingly, they contacted the informants and as per their information, they caught hold of the accused by name Yogaraj, who was proceeding towards Agrahara Dasarahalli, 4th cross and later produced him before CW.16.
He gave Ex.P.6 report.

He has identified the accused No.2.
17.
PW.6 - C.A.Manjappa in his evidence has stated that, while he was working as PSI at Cubbon Park police station, on 20.12.2013 at 1.45 p.m., the PW.1 came to their station and gave Ex.P.1 complaint.
On the basis of which, he registered Ex.P.7 FIR.
On the same day at 2.30 p.m., he visited the spot, which was showed by PW.1 and drawn Ex.P.2 mahazar till 3 p.m., in the presence of PW.3 and CW.4.
KA.05.HK.8723 Hero Honda Splendor motor cycle was traced out by Jagajeevanram Nagar police station.
Hence, the CW.16 forwarded the documents of that vehicle to their station on 20.11.2014 through HC-5630.
That covering letter is marked as Ex.P.8.
Ex. P.9
is the RC seized by CW.16 with respect to KA.06.ED.1436 motor cycle.
On 21.11.2014, he recorded the statement of CW.2.
By completing the investigation, he filed charge sheet against the accused.
18. On the basis of Ex.P.1 written information given by PW.1, the Cubbon park police have registered this case, investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the accused.
In Ex.P.1, the PW.1 has stated that, he owned KA.05.HK.8723 Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle, which he had given to his nephew/ C.Sunil Kumar.

On 17.12.2013 his nephew parked the motorcycle in front of his office,
which is situated at Cunningham cross road.
At 3.30 p.m., when his nephew went to the parking area, he could not find the motorcycle.
They searched for his motorcycle.
His nephew informed the same to him.

Hence, he gave Ex.P.1 complaint to the police and asked them to take necessary legal Nagaraju V vs Mubharak on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144185975/
5 action against the offenders.
19. As per the contents of Ex.P.1, the alleged incident took place on 17.12.2013 in between 1 p.m., to 3.30 p.m. But Ex.P.1 complaint was lodged before the police on 20.12.2013 at 1.45 p.m.
The PW.1 did not explain the reasons as to why there was delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint.

That delay has not been properly explained in Col.3[c] of Ex.P.7 FIR.
20.
In the present case except PW.1 to 3 remaining 3 witnesses are police witnesses.
The PW.1 is the complainant, PW.2 is the circumstantial witness and PW.3 is the mahazar witness.

In the present case, though the prosecution contends that, the accused No.1 stolen the motorcycle from the parking area of Cunningham cross road on 17.12.2013 and handed over the same to accused No.2 and in turn they created forged RC, changed the number plate of the motorcycle and with an intention to cheat the general public they have sold the motorcycle to CW.8 for money and used the fabricated RC as genuine document, it has not produced cogent evidence before the Court to show that the accused No.1 and 2 are the creators of Ex.P.9 RC.
21.

In order to ascertain the correctness of the allegations made against the accused, this court had issued repeated summons, non bailable warrants and proclamations against CW.4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10,
15.
Inspite of it, the prosecution has not secured the presence of those witnesses.
By noting the absence of the witnesses and age of the case, this court dropped them from examination.
22. The PW.6 being the IO did not explain the mahazer under which, KA.05.HK.8723 motor cycle was seized.

No signatories to seizure mahazer i.e., pancha witnesses appeared before the Court to say that, they have seen the police seizing motor cycle and its number plate was changed as KA.06.ED.1436 from KA.05.HK.8723.
23.

Though the prosecution contends that, the accused sold the motor cycle to CW.8 for money by changing its number plate and fabricating RC book, the CW.8, the so-called purchaser has not appeared before the Court to say that, he had purchased the motor cycle from the accused for money.

In order to say that the accused have changed the number plate of Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle from KA.05.HK.8723 to KA.06.ED.1436 by fabricating Ex.P.9 RC and thereby cheated CW.8 and general public, the IO has not collected original RC of that motorcycle so as to compare the chassis number and engine number of that vehicle with chassis number and engine number mentioned in Ex.P.9 fabricated RC.
24.

There is no convincing evidence on record to say that, the accused stolen the motor cycle from the parking area of Cunningham cross road, Bengaluru on the afternoon of 17.12.2013 and they changed its number plate, created Ex.P.9 RC to cheat the public especially CW.8.
The IO did not effectively investigate the matter to know where the duplicate number plate was created and where Ex.P.9 RC was printed.
25. The prosecution contends that, KA.06.ED.1436 motor cycle was seized by Jagajeevanram Nagar police.

As per mahazer dated: 08.08.2014, that motor cycle was seized in the presence of CW.6 to 8.
Nagaraju V vs Mubharak on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144185975/
6 But, none of the pancha witnesses appeared before the Court to say that, they have seen the police seizing KA.06.ED.1436 motor cycle by drawing mahazer in their presence.
26. The PW.1 in his chief examination has stated that, the Cubbon park police called him to the station after a lapse of one year, where he identified his motor cycle.

To the contrary, the PW.2 in his chief examination has stated that, J.J.Nagar police called them to the station on 21.08.2014, where they identified their motor cycle and they found that the number plate of the motor cycle was changed as KA.06.ED.1436.
Hence, a question arises in the mind of the Court, where the PW.1 and 2 actually identified the motor cycle.
27. Neither the PW.1 nor PW.2 stated before the Court that, they have seen the accused or their photos at the station, when they visited to identify the motor cycle.
The evidence led by PW.1 to 6 is no way helpful to the prosecution to hold the accused guilty of the offences charged against them.
The prosecution has not produced convincing evidence before the Court to connect the accused with the alleged crime.
From the evidence led by PW.1 to 6, the charges levelled against the accused are not proved.

28. Thus, the prosecution has failed to prove that, the accused No.1 in furtherance of common intention stolen Hero Honda Splendor motor cycle bearing No.KA.05.HK.8723 of PW.1 on 17.12.2013 in the afternoon, which was parked in the parking area of Cunningham cross road,
Bengaluru and handed over the same to accused No.2, they changed the number of the motor cycle as KA.06.ED.1436, created a RC book by tallying to the chassis and engine number of the motor cycle for the purpose of cheating, dishonestly sold the stolen motor cycle to CW.8 for money, used the forged RC book as a genuine document knowing fully well that, it is a forged document, handed over the same to CW.8 and changed the number plate of the motor cycle with an intention to forge the document.
In such circumstances, I answer point No.1 to 7 in Negative.

Point No.8: For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
By exercising the powers conferred U/Sec.248[1] of Cr.P.C., the accused No.1 and 2 are acquitted from the charge of Sec.379, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 473 R/w 34 of IPC.
The bail bonds executed by the accused stands cancelled.
The bonds executed by the accused No.1 and 2 U/Sec.437[A] of Cr.P.C., will be in force till the completion of appeal period.

The property seized under PF No.124/2014 i.e., Hero Honda Splendor plus motor cycle bearing original No.KA.05.HK. 8723 [ duplicate No. KA. 06.
ED.1436] is already released to the interim custody of PW.1.
That order is made absolute.
